why: All three checks confirm the finding, and a fourth corroborates it. (1) VERBATIM: curl of https://code.claude.com/docs/en/claude-directory.md line 293 carries the tip array element exactly as quoted: 'If a skill and command share a name, the skill takes precedence'. Reading the whole line, the two sibling tips ($ARGUMENTS usage; 'New commands should usually be skills instead; commands remain supported') do not qualify or reverse it. The page is row 77 of scripts/claude-doc-pages.tsv, so it is a valid Claude Code contract page. Independently corroborated on a second page: code.claude.com/docs/en/skills.md and .../slash-commands.md both carry, at line 122, 'If you have files in `.claude/commands/`, those work the same way, but if a skill and a command share the same name, the skill takes precedence.' (2) CODE: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:444 is literally `if (taken.has(skill.logicalName)) continue;`, and the JSDoc at :425-433 states the inverted rule on purpose: '`takenNames` wins: when an explicit command file already provides `/review`, the skill does not also claim that bare name. Explicit commands are authored for this purpose and are the more specific declaration.' (3) CONSEQUENCE, verified separately from the identifier and in the right subsystem: SessionManager.skillSlashCommands (packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16006-16014) forwards takenNames, and BOTH call sites pass `nativeCommands.map(command => command.name)` — the listing path :16039 and the resolution path :16120. `nativeCommands` is loadSessionCustomSlashCommands (:15837), which is discoverCustomSlashCommands over the real .claude/commands/*.md files (plus workflow recipes) — not built-in/native CLI commands, so this is the correct subsystem and not a name collision with a sibling. Nothing upstream reverses it: listCustomSlashCommandSummaries returns [...native, ...plugin, ...skills, ...mcp] with `native` unconditional, the shadowed skill is dropped before the push so it contributes NO entry at all, skillSlashCommandId/`custom:skill:` has no other producer anywhere in packages/ or apps/, and the renderer (AppShell.tsx:1408) only displays the server-supplied list without re-deduping. The behaviour is pinned by tests: custom-commands.test.ts:172-178 asserts `selectSkillSlashCommands([skill('review'), skill('audit')], ['review'])` yields only 'audit', with the comment 'Precedence: an explicit command file wins'. (4) NOT an owner decision: it is not among the nine dated entries in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (seatbelt wildcard, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath, listSessionSummaries), nor in section 4's false positives, and grep finds nothing in the parity audit or the deviation register. It is also not a Nessy product difference (no branding, gateway, or dropped-subscription angle). The only prior record is docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md, which at :427-429 explicitly delegated the choice to the executor ('Decide the precedence between an explicit custom command and a skill-derived one, and state it in the commit body') without citing Claude's docs; tracker row 5 (:568, commit 94cb0f9c) then recorded the chosen direction. That is an undocumented executor choice made against an unread contract, not a reasoned deviation from a known one.
correctedState: Confirmed and inverted relative to the documented contract. Claude Code documents skill-over-command precedence on three pages (claude-directory.md:293; skills.md:122; slash-commands.md:122 — 'if a skill and a command share the same name, the skill takes precedence'). Nessy does the opposite: packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:444 skips any skill whose logicalName is in takenNames, and SessionManager.ts:16039 (listing) and :16120 (resolution) both populate takenNames from the discovered .claude/commands/*.md names (plus workflow-recipe names, which shadow skills the same way — an extra surface Claude does not document). With both commands/review.md and a `review` skill present, exactly one /review exists and it is the command file. One correction to the finding's wording and one to the plan's: the shadowed skill does NOT merely lose its bare alias while keeping a namespaced entry — selectSkillSlashCommands `continue`s before pushing, so it emits no slash command at all, and its custom:skill:review id is therefore unresolvable at SessionManager.ts:16120 too. The skill remains reachable only by model auto-invocation or by the user typing the [skill:review] marker. (The 'keeps only its namespaced custom:skill:<name> id' claim in 2026-07-26-skills-invocation.md:568 is inaccurate; the surviving qualified-key test at custom-commands.test.ts:186-193 covers skill-vs-skill alias shadowing, a different case.) Fixing this means having SessionManager stop feeding native command names into takenNames and instead drop the colliding native command from the listing, so the skill claims the bare /name.
